title: Potato and Pea Samosas with Coriander-Mint Chutney
summary: Crisp, blistered pastry triangles filled with a tempered potato and pea mixture, served warm with a bright coriander and mint chutney.
equipment: wire rack set over a tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
floury potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: Mix the flour and pastry salt, then rub in the 3 tbsp oil with your fingertips until it looks like damp sand. Stir in the yoghurt and enough ice-cold water to form a firm, smooth dough that is not sticky, knead for 1 minute, wrap and rest for 30 minutes. Coating the flour with oil limits gluten, giving a short, crisp crust rather than a chewy one.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potato cubes with cold unsalted water, bring to the boil and simmer for 8-10 minutes until just tender. Drain and leave to steam dry, so the filling stays fluffy rather than wet.

steps.title: Temper the spices
steps.text: Heat the 2 tbsp oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat and add the cumin, fennel and mustard seeds. Fry for 30-60 seconds until the mustard seeds pop, which releases their aromatic oils into the fat. Add the turmeric, chilli flakes and onion and cook for 5-6 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Finish the filling
steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then add the potatoes, peas and filling salt and cook for 3 minutes, lightly crushing some of the potato so the mixture holds together. Off the heat, stir in the coriander and lemon juice, spread out in a bowl and cool completely. Warm filling would soften the pastry and make it tear.

steps.title: Blend the chutney
steps.text: Blend the coriander, mint, green chilli, lemon juice, sugar, chutney salt and water until smooth and bright green. Chill until needed; the acidity of the lemon helps keep the colour vivid.

steps.title: Shape the samosas
steps.text: Divide the pastry into 6 pieces and roll each into an 18 cm round about 2 mm thick, then cut in half. Wet the straight edge of one half, fold it into a cone, overlap and press the seam, then fill with about 2 rounded tbsp filling. Wet the open edge and pinch it firmly closed into a triangle, making 12 in all; any gaps will let oil in.

steps.title: Fry low and slow
steps.text: Heat 5-6 cm of oil in the heavy pot to 160 °C. Fry 3-4 samosas at a time for 8-10 minutes, turning, until blistered, deep golden and crisp, and bring the oil back to 160 °C between batches. Starting cooler keeps the pastry from puffing away from the filling and lets it crisp right through.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Drain on a wire rack and serve warm with the chilled chutney. Resting on a rack rather than paper keeps the bases crisp.

tips: Keep the pastry firm: a soft dough absorbs oil and turns greasy.
The most common mistake is frying too hot, which browns the outside fast and leaves pale, bubbly pastry; use a thermometer and hold 160 °C.
Make the filling a day ahead and chill it; it is easier to shape cold.
safety: Never fill an oil pot more than half full, and lower samosas in gently, away from you.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Refrigerate cooled samosas for up to 2 days and reheat on a tray in a 200 °C (180 °C fan) oven for 10-12 minutes until crisp and piping hot. The chutney keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
